newsitem.title: USA: Phillps backs big Fed financial supervisory role.
newsitem.headline: Phillps backs big Fed financial supervisory role.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Susan Phillips on Wednesday backed consolidated supervision of financial conglomerates and said the central bank needed to play a significant role in that regard.

"In an economy as complicated and integrated as we have in the United States, it is important for the nation's central bank to have a significant role in comprehensive financial institution supervision," Phillips said.
In a speech for delivery to the Exchequer Club here, the Fed policymaker sought to allay concerns that such "umbrella" supervision would be heavy-handed.

"Such oversight need not be overly onerous or intrusive," Phillipis said. "The umbrella supervisor need not attempt to extend bank-like safety and soundness regulations to nonbank entities," she added.

Few, if any, on-site inspections of nonbank affiliates of conglomerates would be necessary, she said. Any visits that were made could be limited to testing the adequacy of management and operating systems in order to protect the conglomerate's banking affiliate, she added.

"While various approaches could be taken to address capital adequacy ... I believe such approaches should be measured against the goal of assuring the safety and soundness of the affiliated banks," Philipps said.
The umbrella supervisor should also have appropriate enforcement authority, including the ability to require the sale of the bank in extreme emergencies, she added.
